questions.question: What is the base URL path for all user-related API endpoints?
questions.explanation: User routes are mounted at '/api/users' as specified in index.js.

questions.question: Which HTTP method is used to create a new todo?
questions.explanation: Creating a new todo uses the POST method to /api/todos endpoint.

questions.question: The API includes input validation for required fields when creating todos.
questions.explanation: The POST /api/todos route validates that user_id, title, and due_date are provided.

questions.question: What HTTP status code is returned when a todo is successfully created?
questions.explanation: The POST /api/todos route returns status 201 (Created) for successful todo creation.

questions.question: Which endpoint is used to get todos for a specific user?
questions.explanation: The route GET /api/todos/user/:userId retrieves all todos for a specific user.

questions.question: The todo routes include comprehensive error handling with try-catch blocks.
questions.explanation: All route handlers in todos.js include try-catch blocks for error handling.

questions.question: What HTTP method is used to mark a todo as completed?
questions.explanation: The PATCH method is used for /api/todos/:id/complete to partially update the completion status.

questions.question: Which route parameter is used to identify a specific user in user routes?
questions.explanation: User routes use :id parameter to identify specific users (e.g., /api/users/:id).

questions.question: The user routes include error handling for database operations.
questions.explanation: User routes in users.js do not include try-catch blocks for error handling.

questions.question: What response format is used when a todo is not found?
questions.explanation: A 404 status with JSON response { error: 'Todo not found' } is returned when a todo is not found.

questions.question: Which endpoint allows updating any field of an existing todo?
questions.explanation: The PUT /api/todos/:id endpoint allows updating any fields of an existing todo.

questions.question: The categories API endpoints are defined in a separate route file.
questions.explanation: Category endpoints are defined directly in index.js, not in a separate route file.

questions.question: What information is returned when successfully deleting a user?
questions.explanation: Delete operations return { success: deleteResult.affectedRows > 0 } format.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code is returned for server errors in todo routes?
questions.explanation: Server errors in todo routes return status 500 (Internal Server Error).

questions.question: The API supports CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) headers.
questions.explanation: The application does not explicitly configure CORS middleware.

questions.question: What type of data does the GET /api/todos endpoint return?
questions.explanation: GET /api/todos returns an array of all todos with associated user information.

questions.question: Which route is used to mark a todo as incomplete?
questions.explanation: The PATCH /api/todos/:id/incomplete route marks a specific todo as incomplete.

questions.question: The user creation endpoint requires an email field.
questions.explanation: The POST /api/users route includes email in the required fields for user creation.

questions.question: What HTTP method is used to completely update a user's information?
questions.explanation: The PUT method is used for /api/users/:id to update user information.

questions.question: Which route provides access to all categories?
questions.explanation: The GET /api/categories endpoint returns all categories from the database.

questions.question: The todo routes validate user permissions before allowing operations.
questions.explanation: There is no authentication or authorization validation in the todo routes.

questions.question: What happens when trying to get a specific category by ID?
questions.explanation: GET /api/categories/:id returns an array containing the category object.

questions.question: Which field is NOT required when creating a new todo?
questions.explanation: The description field is optional when creating a todo; only user_id, title, and due_date are required.

questions.question: The API uses RESTful conventions for endpoint design.
questions.explanation: The API follows RESTful conventions with appropriate HTTP methods and resource-based URLs.

questions.question: What response is returned when successfully updating a todo?
questions.explanation: Update operations return { success: boolean, message: string } format.
